不同观点：
• amai认为Adam Riess的研究及其获得的诺贝尔奖主要依赖于超新星1a作为标准烛光来测量宇宙距离。但如果超新星1a并非标准烛光，且其亮度变化范围更大，那么Riess等人的距离测量结果可能有误。amai认为这种情况的可能性高于其他替代理论，但Riess由于个人原因无法正视这一点。
• tshaddox对文章中将宇宙膨胀的发现归功于1998年Adam Riess的描述感到困惑，指出这是Edwin Hubble在1920年代的发现。
• hn_acc1解释了距离与宇宙膨胀速度的关系，认为更远的星系看起来更快是因为我们看到的是更早期的宇宙状态，而不是现在的状态。
• zvorygin建议记者询问领域内的顶尖科学家，在得知Hubble张力之前和之后，他们对标准模型正确性的看法，以便更清晰地了解情况。
• pavel_lishin对宇宙学研究感到兴奋，将其与19世纪和1930年代的科学突破相提并论。
• gaoshan将宇宙膨胀比作爆炸扩展，认为这可能是最接近的类比。
• jgalt212认为暗能量和暗物质像是“修补因素”，对其持怀疑态度。
• daedrdev提醒大家注意，尽管诺贝尔奖得主有很高的学术声望，但有些人也会有偏离主流科学观点的情况，因此不能完全依赖诺贝尔奖得主的观点。

补充讨论：
• 评论中提到了对超新星1a作为标准烛光的可靠性的质疑，这是讨论的核心争议点。
• 对宇宙膨胀的理解和描述存在不同解释，例如爆炸扩展的类比。
• 对科学研究中的权威性和怀疑态度的讨论，特别是诺贝尔奖得主的观点是否应被无条件接受。
• 对具体研究结果和测量方法的技术性讨论，例如距离与速度的关系。
• 对文章内容的技术性细节和表述方式的关注，如tshaddox对文章时间线的困惑。

这些观点反映了科学界内外的不同声音，既有对具体科学问题的深入探讨，也有对科学权威性和研究方法的反思。

data.article_summary: Station Display是一款显示瑞士公共交通时刻表的设备，具备实时数据更新功能，可显示当前站点的下次发车时间及延误信息。设备采用铝制外壳和染色有机玻璃，设计现代。其192 x 64像素的LED显示屏在日夜均清晰可见，并提供多种主题选择。设备支持壁挂或桌面摆放，可通过Android或iOS应用配置，并具备开放API供自定义数据源。需要2.4 GHz Wi-Fi和电源支持，适用于室内环境。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对一个新的交通信息显示设备/应用的可行性、功能和局限性进行讨论。

不同观点：
• [支持并感兴趣] @sureglymop 认为该设备非常实用，能够解决其日常查看公交车发车时间的需求，并建议增加对船只、缆车及跨境火车的支持，还提出可以添加NFC标签以方便购票。
• [技术联想] @1shooner 联想到一个类似的项目（metrobox），提供了技术项目的参考链接，表明类似的技术已经存在，并可能为该讨论提供了更多背景信息。
• [功能扩展建议] @throwaway81523 认为该功能可以集成到手机应用中，并指出仅显示发车时间不够，还需要显示列车/公交的实时位置和到达时间，尤其是乘客已经在车上或需要接人时。

• [实用性担忧] @busymom0 对外部使用限制（"仅限室内使用"）表示担忧，并要求 clarification 关于该设备/应用的具体用途。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于该设备的实际用途与局限性，特别是其仅限于室内使用和地域性限制是否合理。
• 另一个讨论焦点是功能的全面性，尤其是实时位置和到达时间的需求未被满足，用户认为现有的应用在这方面做得不够。

data.title: Human coders are still better than LLMs
data.author: longwave
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）在编程和软件工程中的应用及未来影响

不同观点：
• LLM作为辅助工具的价值：[mattnewton]认为LLM像一个智能的橡皮鸭，可以帮助梳理思路并在一定程度上优化代码。这种辅助功能在当前具有价值，但未来两年是否依然如此尚不确定。
• LLM的快速进步：[UncleOxidant]指出LLM在过去几年中取得了巨大进步，尽管目前存在一些不足，但预计未来仍会有所改善。他批评了一些人尚未尝试就对LLM持否定态度。
• 人类程序员的价值：[ChrisMarshallNY]强调优秀程序员的不可替代性，尤其是像他提到的日本工程师那样具有深厚技术功底的人。LLM在处理复杂问题时难以超越优秀的人类程序员。
• 软件工程的社会和需求分析方面：[yua_mikami]认为编写代码只是软件工程的一部分，更重要的部分是与客户沟通、需求分析等社会性任务，这些是LLM难以胜任的。
• LLM在特定任务中的优势：[wanderingstan]指出LLM在某些重复性任务（如CSS语法或库调用）上表现出色，能显著提高效率。
• LLM对企业的长期和短期影响：[loudmax]认为利用LLM提高生产力的公司会成功，而试图完全取代员工的公司会失败。短期内一些公司可能因错误策略而牺牲未来增长。
• 商业世界对软件质量的影响：[acquisitionsilk]担心商业世界对利润的追求会导致软件质量下降，开发者的努力可能无法改变这一趋势。
• LLM取代程序员的可能性：[am17an]认为程序员应该注意到技术发展的趋势，并为可能的未来做好准备。LLM和其他AI技术有可能取代部分编程工作。
• 开发者被商品化和LLM的替代：[austin-cheney]认为许多开发者因自我商品化而容易被LLM取代，过去25年中开发者自身的职业态度导致了这一局面。
• LLM无法处理的复杂决策：[solatic]指出编写代码涉及复杂的权衡决策，LLM无法独立完成这些决策，仍需人类提供上下文和指导。
• LLM的实际使用体验：[smilbandit]发现LLM有时会有帮助，但也会干扰工作流程，需要人工审查和调整生成的代码。
• LLM的局限性和错误：[bouncycastle]分享了自己使用LLM失败的经历，指出LLM在处理复杂任务时会出现“幻觉”和错误，仍需人类专家介入。
• LLM在处理大型项目中的不足：[frogperson]认为LLM难以处理涉及大量上下文和复杂逻辑的大型软件项目，目前其能力范围有限。
• 人类抽象思维和创造力的不可替代性：[bdbenton5255]强调人类在设计和解决创造性问题上的独特能力，LLM可以模仿人类生成代码，但无法替代人类的抽象思维和项目构建能力。

补充讨论：
• LLM是否只能达到平均水平：[pupppet]质疑LLM仅通过模式匹配是否只能达到平均水平，而无法真正擅长某一领域。

争议焦点：
• LLM能否在未来取代人类程序员，尤其是在处理复杂项目和社会性任务方面存在争议。一部分人认为LLM有潜力取代部分编程工作，而另一些人则强调人类程序员的独特价值和复杂决策能力不可替代。
• LLM的快速进步是否足以应对当前软件工程的全部需求，以及其在实际应用中的局限性和错误处理能力也是争议的焦点。

data.title: 'He spent thousands': how a bank team tries to rescue scam victims
data.author: jplrssn
data.article_summary: 自新冠疫情以来，诈骗活动的数量和复杂性大幅上升。文章介绍了桑坦德银行的“破咒”（Break the Spell）团队，该团队专门负责拯救被诈骗犯欺骗的客户，尤其是陷入“恋爱诈骗”的受害者。团队有23名成员，处理那些深陷骗局、拒绝承认被骗的客户，通常这些客户已被骗子通过虚假投资或恋爱承诺骗取了积蓄。团队通过多次耐心沟通，尝试赢得客户信任并阻止他们继续被骗。例如，一位丧偶的退休老人坚信一个从未见面的女子会搬来与他同居，尽管银行多次阻止付款，他仍不愿相信这是骗局。文章还提到，根据新规，银行必须赔偿未疏忽大意的受害者，因此银行正加紧保护客户资金。自2021年成立以来，该团队已成功阻止了1760万英镑被骗走。

44137241.article_content:
The prevalence and complexity of scams has soared since the Covid pandemic.
Composite: Alex Mellon for the Guardian : Getty Images
View image in fullscreen
The prevalence and complexity of scams has soared since the Covid pandemic.
Composite: Alex Mellon for the Guardian : Getty Images
Scams
This article is more than
3 months old
‘He spent thousands’: how a bank team tries to rescue scam victims
This article is more than 3 months old
Santander’s specialist squad aims to save customers from the grips of fraudsters offering romance and more
Anna Tims
Sat 1 Feb 2025 04.12 EST
Last modified on Sun 2 Feb 2025 04.03 EST
Share
A
widowed pensioner is on the end of the phone and he’s flustered. He’s expecting his girlfriend to move in with him next month. He has never met her, but he has photos of a young blonde woman and weeks of texts pledging her devotion.
On an industrial estate in Bootle on Merseyside, Clare is trying to deflate his dreams. She is a call handler on Santander’s Break the Spell team, which is part of the high street bank’s fraud prevention department. It is her job to convince the man that his girlfriend is actually a scammer who has defrauded him of his savings.
Fraudsters stole more than £30m from Santander customers last year by conning them into making payments for fake goods or services. Across the UK banking sector as a whole £213m of customers’ money was lost to scams where people were tricked into sending money to bank accounts operated by criminals in the first six months of 2024, according to the trade body UK Finance.
View image in fullscreen
The 23 staff on the Break the Spell team deal with customers who have been so thoroughly taken in by a scam that they refuse to accept that they are being defrauded.
Photograph: EnVogue_Photo/Alamy
The prevalence and complexity of scams has soared since the pandemic, and so has the financial hit to banks and building societies. Many were signed up to a voluntary industry scheme to reimburse victims who were not unduly negligent, but
new rules introduced in October
have made such refunds mandatory, so there is a new urgency for banks to protect their customers’ savings.
The 23 staff on the Break the Spell team deal with customers who have been so thoroughly taken in by a scam that they refuse to accept they are being defrauded. Most of them have been bamboozled into paying their savings into fake investment schemes or the pockets of criminal gangs who woo them online and promise romance. They are referred to Break the Spell by the bank’s fraud contact centre once ordinary interventions fail to persuade them that their transactions are suspect, and it is up to the team to win their trust and save them from themselves. It can take months.
Clare is not making headway with the widower. She has been calling him regularly for a fortnight. His payments to the woman have been blocked by the bank, and Clare has urged him to discuss his plans with family members, but the scammer has convinced him their relationship must be kept secret.
He has already sent thousands of pounds in response to her sob stories and promises. He recently travelled across the UK for a rendezvous with his intended, but she did not show up and had an emotional excuse at the ready.
On Clare’s computer screen are images of the woman upon whom the man has pinned his hopes. A reverse image search – an easy way to find out if photos have appeared on the internet – shows them replicated under different names across myriad social media sites – evidence that scammers are using them to woo victims.
View image in fullscreen
One elderly man was defrauded of his savings by a scammer he was convinced was about to move in with him.
Photograph: Westend61/Getty Images
The man, however, is not ready to accept that he is a victim. Clare urges him to visit his local bank branch and perform a reverse image search himself, but he stalls. He will wait until next month, he says. By then, he hopes his new life will have started.
“Romance scams can go on for years, and if you’re calling from the bank and telling them their wife-to-be isn’t real, you have to be really sensitive,” Clare said. “Last week he finally accepted that he was being scammed, but then she worked on him and now he’s back in deep.”
The UK’s
Banking Protocol
scheme encourages staff to involve the police if they believe a customer needs protection from criminal activity, and officers will be sent to the widower’s home if he ceases contact for more than a week.

data.author: adam_gyroscope
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了WeatherStar 4000+系统（版本5.21.8）的天气预报界面。用户可以查看当前天气状况和每小时预报，包括温度、风力、云量和降水概率。此外，还提供旅行预报、区域观测、日出日落时间、风暴预测和雷达信息等。用户可以访问各种天气数据和设置，并能分享和复制预报链接。文章还列出了地点、监测站和雷达的ID信息。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：复古天气频道图形生成设备WeatherStar 4000的复兴以及相关技术、文化和情感讨论

不同观点：
• **技术复原与怀旧**：[ndiddy]和[post_break]介绍了通过重写固件让WeatherStar 4000恢复90年代天气报告图形的技术项目，包括使用Raspberry Pi和3D打印屏幕模拟CRT显示。这引发了对复古技术怀旧价值的讨论。[doawoo]和[ZYbCRq22HbJ2y7]则补充了相关软件资源和代码链接。

• **音乐与情感联系**：[gasgiant]和[jader201]分享了对90年代天气频道背景音乐的情感联系，提到了Pat Metheny Group和The Rippingtons等音乐。这表明天气频道不仅仅是天气信息，还带有特定时代的情感共鸣。

• **对现代天气频道的不满**：[bdbenton5255]和[theturtle]表达了对现代天气频道的不满，认为其失去了过去的人情味和专业性，批评了现代频道过多的非天气内容和商业化趋势。

• **技术实现与应用**：[socalgal2]期待更先进的天气频道模拟技术，比如AI生成天气预报视频。[jasonpeacock]则从用户体验角度提出了对当前项目的改进建议，比如书签功能和退出全屏模式的快捷键。[disposition2]寻求将该项目通过VLC流媒体播放的技术指导。

补充讨论：
• **项目影响与文化意义**：[gdubs]和[DigiEggz]认为该项目不仅是技术的复原，更是唤起了人们对过去美好时光的回忆，强调了其文化价值和怀旧意义。

• **历史技术细节**：[catgirlinspace]回忆了"Local on the 8s"的实现方式，描述了在DirecTV上通过信号生成静态图像的技术细节，提供了对过去技术运作方式的深入理解。

争议焦点：
• **现代天气频道质量下降**：一些评论者如[theturtle]对现代天气频道的变化表示不满，认为其偏离了原本的专业性，加入了过多的商业元素和不必要的噱头。

整体来看，讨论围绕技术复兴、怀旧情感、现代不满和未来改进展开，展现了对过去技术的怀念和对未来技术发展的期待。

data.title: Ask HN: Lisp eval vs. Lisp macros. Are they the same underlying concept?
data.author: behnamoh
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Lisp中宏（macros）的作用和用途

不同观点：
• **[uticus的观点]**：提供相关学习资源链接，但没有明确表达个人立场，倾向于引导读者查阅外部资料以深入理解。

• **[timonoko的观点]**：
  - 认为如果开发者需要询问宏的用途，那么他们实际上并不需要使用宏。
  - 宏的主要作用是给编译器提供指令，以加快编译速度。
  - 认为宏在语法改进方面的作用很小，因为Lisp本身几乎没有实际的语法结构。

• **[andsoitis的观点]**：
  - 详细区分了`eval`和宏，强调两者虽然都涉及“代码即数据”的概念，但在程序生命周期中的作用和运行时间不同。
  - `eval`在运行时执行，接受数据结构并作为Lisp代码进行评估，适用于在程序运行过程中动态构建和执行代码。
  - 宏在编译时运行，用于在代码评估之前进行转换，返回新的代码形式供后续编译或评估使用。
  - 宏可以用于扩展语言，定义新的语法结构，支持创建强大的领域特定语言（DSL）和优化代码。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：timonoko认为宏的主要作用是加速编译，而andsoitis则强调宏在扩展语言和创建DSL方面的强大功能，这表明对宏用途的理解存在分歧。

• **重要论据**：
  - timonoko的论据集中在宏对编译器的指令作用和Lisp缺乏传统语法的特性。
  - andsoitis提供了具体的例子和详细的解释，区分了`eval`和宏的不同用途和运行时间，突出了宏在编译时的转换作用。

• **讨论深度**：andsoitis的评论提供了更深入的技术分析和实例，相比之下，timonoko的观点更为简洁，且带有一些主观判断。

data.title: Bret Victor's Refs
data.author: pramodbiligiri
data.article_summary: 这篇文章列出了从1828年到1977年一系列重要的科学和技术文献，涵盖数学分析、通信理论、计算机科学、人工智能、教育和心理学等多个领域。关键文献包括Green的《数学分析的应用》、Nyquist的《影响电报速度的因素》、Bush的《微分分析仪》和Turing的《可计算数及其在判定问题中的应用》。文章还涵盖了Shannon的《通信的数学理论》、Maslow的《人类动机理论》以及McCulloch的《神经活动中的逻辑计算》。此外，还涉及Bush的《如我们所想》和Engelbart的《增强人类智力》。这些文献对现代计算机科学、人工智能和信息理论的发展具有重要影响。

data.title: Memvid – Video-Based AI Memory
data.author: sunbum
data.article_summary: Memvid是一个基于视频的AI记忆库，通过将文本数据编码为视频文件，实现对大规模文本数据的快速语义搜索和即时检索。它无需传统数据库，可将数百万文本块压缩存储在一个MP4文件中，并支持自然语言查询和内置聊天功能。Memvid还具有高效存储、支持PDF导入、离线使用和简单API等特点，适用于数字图书馆、教育内容、新闻档案、企业知识库和研究论文等场景。安装和使用简单，通过几行代码即可创建可搜索的视频记忆库并进行语义搜索。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于“耶稣是否会在今年回归”的预测市场评论，涵盖信仰、市场操作、技术争议等多个角度。

不同观点：
• blendergeek认为，真正的信仰者不会参与这种赌注，因为他们相信世界末日到来时，世俗的事情（如预测市场）将不再有意义。因此，他认为参与“是的”赌注的人并不是真的相信耶稣会回归。
• JohnMakin则通过之前类似的市场案例（如“希拉里是否会参选”）说明，市场中可能存在大量投机者利用短期新闻波动进行交易，而不全是真正的信仰者。
• k310从宗教和社会的角度出发，认为即使耶稣回归，他的教义在当今社会也不会被广泛接受，因为现代社会的许多经济和政治基础与耶稣的教义背道而驰。
• legitster指出，这种市场反映了美国某些新教神学（如 dispensationalism）的影响，这些神学强调世界的恶化和耶稣突然回归的可能性，这与市场参与者的信仰密切相关。

补充讨论：
• ecocentrik认为，市场的真正目的是吸引关注和交易量，而不是讨论耶稣是否回归。市场创建者的可信度和解决方案标准是关键问题。
• thatjoeoverthr提出，即使耶稣回归，人们也不会一致相信，且可以通过操纵让人们相信耶稣已经回归。还提到“Deep Fake耶稣”的可能性。
• Nevermark指出，Polymarket有强烈的动机提供有趣的长赔率赌注，以吸引资金和关注，这是一种免费的公关策略。
• throw7对“可信来源的共识”如何决定市场结果表示质疑，并希望了解具体来源和共识的标准。

• dweez将购买“是的”一方比作宏观经济赌注，类似于短期国债。

• yabones幽默地提到要通过帕斯卡的赌注来计算这个赌注的价值。
• ddp26对预测市场中大量智力活动用于套利和边缘案例研究表示失望，认为AI可能比人类众包更适合预测市场。
• keeganpoppen认为，市场的价格不仅反映价值，还受到时间价值的影响，并提出如何建模这种偏好的问题。

争议焦点：
• 市场的真实目的和操纵可能性，尤其是市场创建者的可信度和解决方案标准。

44112686.article_content:
Eric Neyman
Prediction markets
,
Predictions
March 24, 2025
Thanks to Jesse Richardson for discussion.
Polymarket asks:
will Jesus Christ return in 2025?
In the three days since the market opened, traders have wagered over $100,000 on this question. The market traded as high as 5%, and is now stably trading at 3%. Right now, if you wanted to, you could place a bet that Jesus Christ will not return this year, and earn over $13,000 if you’re right.
There are two mysteries here: an easy one, and a harder one.
The easy mystery is: if people are willing to bet $13,000 on “Yes”, why isn’t anyone taking them up?
The answer is that, if you wanted to do that, you’d have to put down over $1 million of your own money, locking it up inside Polymarket through the end of the year. At the end of that year, you’d get 1% returns on your investment. And you can do
so much
better on the stock market, or even in U.S. treasury bonds.
So that’s why no one is buying the market down to 1%. But the real mystery is: why is anyone participating in the market on the “Yes” side? Like, who is betting that Jesus
will
return this year, and why?
Here are a few answers I came up with:
[True Believers] Maybe these people really believe that there’s a 3% chance that Christ will return this year!
[Incorrect Resolution] Maybe the “Yes” people are betting that the market will be resolved incorrectly (that there’s a 3% chance that the market will resolve “Yes” even though Christ will not return in 2025).
[The Memes] Maybe the “Yes” people are buying “Yes” for the lulz. It’s kinda fun to tell people that you bet that Jesus Christ would return this year!
But none of these hypotheses ring true to me:
The True Believers hypothesis rings false because that would be a frankly ridiculous belief to hold. Sometimes people profess ridiculous things, but very few of them put their money where their mouth is on prediction markets.
1
The Incorrect Resolution hypothesis rings false because, while there’s some chance of an incorrect resolution, it’s really unlikely to be as high as 3%. Polymarket has a lot of reputation to lose by incorrectly resolving this market, and would almost certainly override its
consensus-based resolution mechanism
if it came to that.
The Memes hypothesis is more plausible, but I think ultimately false. Several people have spent hundreds of dollars betting yes, which is a lot of money to spend for the memes.
So I asked my friend Jesse, who trades on Polymarket, and he had a pretty interesting theory:
[Time Value of Money] The Yes people are betting that, later this year, their counterparties (the No betters) will want cash (to bet on other markets), and so will sell out of their No positions at a higher price.
In other words: right now, there’s not much interesting stuff happening on Polymarket. People are spending a lot of money betting on sports, but not much else. But at some point in 2025, other markets will get a lot of attention. The
New York mayoral election
is happening this year. Pope Francis is in poor health, so there may be a
new pope
this year. God forbid
China invade Taiwan
, but such an invasion would result in many interesting markets. Right now, all these markets have mere single-digit millions of dollars in trading volume, but that could very easily change.
And if it changes, some of the people betting No on Christ’s return will want to unlock that money — that is, sell their “No” shares — so that they can use it to bet on other markets. If enough people want to sell their “No” shares, the “Yes” holders may be able to sell out at an elevated price, like 6%, potentially getting a 2x return on their investment!
The Time Value of Money hypothesis posits that the Yes bettors are more sophisticated than they look. In finance,
time value of money
is the idea that a dollar today is worth more than a dollar tomorrow, because you can do things with that dollar, such as making bets. The Yes traders are betting that the time value of Polymarket cash will go up unexpectedly: that other traders will be short on cash to place bets with, and will at some point be willing to pay a premium to free up the cash that they spent betting against Jesus.
Has this galaxy-brained trade ever gone well? Yes! In late October of last year — a week before the election — Kamala Harris was trading around 0.3% in safe red states like Kentucky, while Donald Trump was trading around 0.3% in safe blue states like Massachusetts. On election day, these prices
skyrocketed
to about 1.5%, because “No” bettors desperately needed cash to place other bets on the election. Traders who bought “Yes” for 0.3% in late October and sold at 1.5% on election day made a 5x profit! This means that even though Harris only had a 0.1% chance
2
of winning Kentucky, the “correct” price for the Kentucky market to trade at was more like 1.5%.
This means that the Jesus Christ market is quite interesting! You could make it even more interesting by replacing it with “This Market Wil

data.author: Elliott-Diy
data.article_summary: Weather2Geo是一款开源OSINT工具，通过分析泄露的天气小部件数据（时间、温度、天气状况）进行地理定位。它使用与Windows天气小部件相同的API，将截图中的天气信息与真实城市匹配，实现地理定位。该工具具有时区感知、聚类分析和可扩展性等特点，适用于短时间内处理截图数据。安装和使用需要通过Git克隆项目并运行Python脚本，输入截图中的时间、天气和温度等信息，工具会返回符合条件的城市集群。该工具仅限于合法的OSINT和教育用途，强调尊重隐私和法律界限。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何缩小问题空间以及数据处理的长期维护

不同观点：
• **landgenoot** 认为可以通过解析日期和时间格式来缩小问题空间，并提供了一个维基百科链接，列出了不同国家的日期格式。这表明他关注的是技术实现中的具体细节问题，尤其是如何处理多种多样的日期格式以提高系统的准确性。

• **progbits** 则更关心数据的长期维护和历史数据库的建立，提出了是否计划抓取数据并维护一个历史数据库的问题。他还提到了使用旧截图数据的可能性，同时指出了在实现这一目标时可能遇到的困难，特别是突破速率限制（rate limits）的挑战。

补充讨论：
- **landgenoot** 的观点侧重于技术细节，尤其是通过标准化或识别不同的日期格式来简化问题。
- **progbits** 的观点则更具战略性，考虑了数据的历史保存和长期使用价值，同时指出了技术实现中的潜在障碍，如速率限制等实际问题。
- 争议的焦点可能在于优先级的不同：landgenoot 更关注技术实现的细节，而 progbits 则着眼于系统的长期可持续性和扩展性。

总结：
• 技术实现细节：解析日期和时间格式以缩小问题空间。
• 长期数据维护：抓取数据并建立历史数据库的必要性和挑战。
• 争议焦点：技术细节与长期战略之间的优先级选择。

Weather2Geo
If you find this project useful, please consider leaving a ⭐, it helps others discover the tool and supports continued development.
Overview
Weather2Geo
is a focused OSINT tool that turns weather widget leaks into geolocation data.
People post screenshots with the Windows weather widget in their taskbar all the time, showing the exact temperature, weather condition, and local time. This tool uses the same API as the widget to find cities where those conditions are currently true.
⚠️
This tool works best if used shortly after the screenshot is posted. Conditions change fast.
Features
Geolocation from Widgets
: Match weather condition, temp, and time to a list of real cities
Timezone-Aware
: Localizes your input to each city’s timezone for accurate comparison
Clustering
: Groups nearby hits to reduce noise
Extensible
: Tweak tolerance, data sources, and clustering distance
Installation
git clone https://github.com/elliott-diy/Weather2Geo
cd
Weather2Geo
pip install -r requirements.txt
Usage
python main.py run --time
"
2025-05-22 14:00
"
--condition
"
Mostly cloudy
"
--temp 18 --tolerance 1.0
Options
Flag
Description
--time
Local time shown in the screenshot (
YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM
)
--condition
Weather condition string (e.g., "Partly cloudy")
--temp
Temperature in Celsius
--tolerance
Temp wiggle room (default: 1.0°C)
--cluster-distance
Max distance in KM to group hits (default: 15)
--cities-file
Path to GeoNames cities file (default:
cities15000.txt
)
Example Use Case
You spot a screenshot that says:
Mostly clear | 13°C | 10:09 PM | May 22
Run:
python main.py run --time
"
2025-05-22 22:09
"
--condition
"
Mostly clear
"
--temp 13
And you'll get clusters of cities like:
Cluster 1 – 10 locations:
- US Seattle — 13°C, mostly clear
- US Bellevue — 13°C, mostly clear
...
Data Sources
City List
:
GeoNames
cities15000.txt
Weather
:
MSN Weather API
— same backend as the Windows widget
Contributing
Found a bug? Want to improve matching accuracy or add new data sources? Pull requests are welcome!
Feel free to:
Open an
issue
with suggestions or bugs
Submit a PR for improvements (accuracy, timezone logic, clustering, etc.)
Share how you’re using the tool - feedback helps guide future features
Disclaimer
This tool is for ethical, educational OSINT use only. Don’t be a creep. Respect privacy and legal boundaries.

• **landgenoot** 认为可以通过解析日期和时间格式来缩小问题空间，并提供了一个维基百科链接，列出了不同国家的日期格式。这表明他关注的是技术实现中的具体细节问题，尤其是如何处理多种多样的日期格式以提高系统的准确性。

• **progbits** 则更关心数据的长期维护和历史数据库的建立，提出了是否计划抓取数据并维护一个历史数据库的问题。他还提到了使用旧截图数据的可能性，同时指出了在实现这一目标时可能遇到的困难，特别是突破速率限制（rate limits）的挑战。

补充讨论：
- **landgenoot** 的观点侧重于技术细节，尤其是通过标准化或识别不同的日期格式来简化问题。
- **progbits** 的观点则更具战略性，考虑了数据的历史保存和长期使用价值，同时指出了技术实现中的潜在障碍，如速率限制等实际问题。
- 争议的焦点可能在于优先级的不同：landgenoot 更关注技术实现的细节，而 progbits 则着眼于系统的长期可持续性和扩展性。

总结：
• 技术实现细节：解析日期和时间格式以缩小问题空间。
• 长期数据维护：抓取数据并建立历史数据库的必要性和挑战。
• 争议焦点：技术细节与长期战略之间的优先级选择。

typed-ffmpeg
typed-ffmpeg
offers a modern, Pythonic interface to FFmpeg, providing extensive support for complex filters with detailed typing and documentation. Inspired by
ffmpeg-python
, this package enhances functionality by addressing common limitations, such as lack of IDE integration and comprehensive typing, while also introducing new features like JSON serialization of filter graphs and automatic FFmpeg validation.
Table of Contents
Features
Installation
Quick Usage
Documentation
Interactive Playground
Acknowledgements
Features
Zero Dependencies:
Built purely with the Python standard library, ensuring maximum compatibility and security.
User-Friendly:
Simplifies the construction of filter graphs with an intuitive Pythonic interface.
Comprehensive FFmpeg Filter Support:
Out-of-the-box support for most FFmpeg filters, with IDE auto-completion.
Integrated Documentation:
In-line docstrings provide immediate reference for filter usage, reducing the need to consult external documentation.
Robust Typing:
Offers static and dynamic type checking, enhancing code reliability and development experience.
Filter Graph Serialization:
Enables saving and reloading of filter graphs in JSON format for ease of use and repeatability.
Graph Visualization:
Leverages
graphviz
for visual representation, aiding in understanding and debugging.
Validation and Auto-correction:
Assists in identifying and fixing errors within filter graphs.
Input and Output Options Support:
Provide a more comprehensive interface for input and output options, including support for additional codecs and formats.
Partial Evaluation:
Enhance the flexibility of filter graphs by enabling partial evaluation, allowing for modular construction and reuse.
Planned Features
Please note that the following features are under consideration or development for future releases:
Extended FFmpeg Version Support:
While
typed-ffmpeg
is currently built with FFmpeg version 6.0 in mind, we are working to ensure compatibility across different FFmpeg versions. Feedback and issue reports are welcome to improve version support.
Additional Filter Support:
We aim to expand the range of FFmpeg filters supported by
typed-ffmpeg
. Continuous updates will be made to include more complex and varied filters.
Installation
To install
typed-ffmpeg
, simply use pip:
pip install typed-ffmpeg
Note: FFmpeg must be installed on your system.
Note: If you need to install
ffmpeg-python
at the same time, use
pip install typed-ffmpeg-compatible
to prevent conflicts with the module name.​

'
typed-ffmpeg[graph]
'

data.title: Surprisingly fast AI-generated kernels we didn't mean to publish yet
data.author: mfiguiere
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了意外生成的非常快速的AI生成CUDA内核，这些内核在某些情况下甚至超过了PyTorch中专家优化过的生产内核。关键结果包括：Matmul (FP32) 性能达到torch.matmul的101.3%；Conv2D性能达到torch.nn.Conv2D的179.9%；Softmax性能达到torch.softmax的111.8%；LayerNorm性能达到torch.nn.LayerNorm的484.4%；以及Conv2D + ReLU + MaxPool的性能达到参考值的290.1%。这些内核是使用简单的合成数据生成方法意外获得的，该方法通过自然语言推理优化想法并行生成多个代码变体，从而避免了传统顺序修正中的局部最小问题。文章强调了这种方法在性能内核生成方面的潜力，并视为未来探索的第一步。

44139454.article_content:
Surprisingly Fast AI-Generated Kernels We Didn’t Mean to Publish (Yet)
Authors:
Anne Ouyang and
Azalia Mirhoseini and
Percy Liang
TL;DR
We have some very fast AI-generated kernels in pure CUDA-C without using libraries and DSLs such as CUTLASS and Triton. They are performing close to or in some cases even beating the standard expert-optimized production kernels shipped in PyTorch. Some of our highlighted results:
Matmul (FP32): 101.3%
performance of FP32 torch.matmul; problem size: 4096x4096 square matrices
Conv2D: 179.9%
performance of FP32 torch.nn.Conv2D; problem size: (100, 3, 224, 224) input tensor, conv(in_channels=3, out_channels=96, kernel_size=11, stride=4, padding=2)
Softmax: 111.8%
performance of FP32 torch.softmax; problem size: (4096, 65536) input tensor
LayerNorm: 484.4%
performance of FP32 torch.nn.LayerNorm; problem size: (16, 64, 256, 256) input tensor
Conv2D + ReLU + MaxPool: 290.1%
performance of FP32 torch reference, 189.0% performance of FP32 torch.compile() reference; problem size: (100, 3, 224, 224) input tensor, conv(in_channels=3, out_channels=96, kernel_size=11, stride=4, padding=2), maxpool(kernel_size=3, stride=2)
(Our results are benchmarked on an Nvidia L40S GPU, and % performance is defined as reference time divided by generated kernel time)
“Untiled” by DALL·E (2025). (Digital pigment on virtual canvas)
From the MMA collection
Intro
We started with the goal of generating synthetic data to train better kernel generation models. Somewhere along the way the unexpected happened: the test-time only synthetic data generation itself started producing
really
good kernels beating or performing close to human expert optimized PyTorch baselines, utilizing advanced optimizations and hardware features, which were previously thought to be challenging. As a result, we decided to write this blog post early and share our findings. The point of this blog post isn’t about a novel methodology; in fact, our synthetic data generation design is simple, and what’s surprising is that it is already showing promise.
In this post, we’re sharing the method, five optimized kernels (4 foundational ML operators + 1 fused kernel of an AlexNet block), an example optimization trajectory, and some takeaways and thoughts on what this might mean for performant kernel generation. Consider this a first step in what’s next.
Method
We’re using the
KernelBench
(a benchmark for AI based kernel generation that we released in December 2024) task setup: given torch code, the LLM writes custom kernels to replace the torch operators with the goal of getting a speedup. Consistent with the original KernelBench design, the reference code is in the default FP32, and given a tolerance threshold (1e-02), using lower precision solutions is valid. In addition, each problem in KernelBench has specific sizes since there are many size-specific optimizations, so the benchmark tests for the fastest kernel for the specific problem size, not necessarily a generally fast kernel for any arbitrary problem size. We run both the torch reference code and the generated code, and test for correctness by checking the numerical equality of the two outputs over many random inputs.
The most common way people scale test-time compute for this problem of optimizing kernels today is through sequential revision, a multi-turn loop where a model incrementally edits a kernel, checks for correctness and performance, then tries again based on the result, either fixing the kernel or try to improve its performance. This loop is intuitive and easy to implement. The model fixes broken kernels, tweaks working ones, and gradually climbs toward something faster.
The main limitation of this approach is the lack of optimization idea diversity. Sequential loops often fall into local minima, revisiting the same classes of transformations or endlessly refining unpromising trajectories. The result is inefficient use of test-time compute and little pressure on the model to generate fundamentally new optimization ideas.
We introduced two key changes to address this:
Reasoning in natural language about optimization ideas: rather than directly generating new kernels in each step, we generate optimization ideas in natural language conditioned on previously attempted ideas, and realize those ideas into new code variants.
Branching at each optimization step: instead of refining a single candidate per step, we fan out such that each idea spawns multiple implementations, and the highest-performing kernels are used to seed the next round (we also keep a bank of good existing kernels for seeding). This unlocks massive parallelism allowing us to explore radically different directions at each turn, rather than getting stuck in a narrow optimization path.
The result is a test-time loop that looks less like “chat with a compiler” in the case of sequential revision, and more like structured exploratory search, guided by explicit optimization hypotheses and aggressively parallel evaluation
44139454.article_summary: 文章介绍了意外生成的非常快速的AI生成CUDA内核，这些内核在某些情况下甚至超过了PyTorch中专家优化过的生产内核。关键结果包括：Matmul (FP32) 性能达到torch.matmul的101.3%；Conv2D性能达到torch.nn.Conv2D的179.9%；Softmax性能达到torch.softmax的111.8%；LayerNorm性能达到torch.nn.LayerNorm的484.4%；以及Conv2D + ReLU + MaxPool的性能达到参考值的290.1%。这些内核是使用简单的合成数据生成方法意外获得的，该方法通过自然语言推理优化想法并行生成多个代码变体，从而避免了传统顺序修正中的局部最小问题。文章强调了这种方法在性能内核生成方面的潜力，并视为未来探索的第一步。
44139454.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕AI生成代码（特别是AI生成的OS kernel和LLM优化）的讨论，包括性能、方法论及其潜在影响。

不同观点：
• [miki123211] 认为AI代理应被视为“任务”或“工作”，而不是像人类员工那样局限于一次执行一个任务。他们提出，LLM的优势在于可以随时生成无限数量的代理，并且并行执行任务没有额外的成本优势。
• [ekelsen] 指出，FP32在现代ML工作负载中不如FP16或BF16常见，且由于缺乏优化，因此在FP32上获得性能提升并不令人惊讶。他们认为更值得关注的是那些已经被开发者优化过的常见数据类型和内核。
• [thorum] 从多个来源（包括Google的AlphaEvolve和o3发现Linux内核漏洞）得出结论，Gemini Pro 2.5和o3已经达到了新的能力水平，使得过去不成功的想法现在能够成功实现。
• [userbinator] 表示最初以为文章是关于AI生成一个操作系统内核，暗示对文章标题或宣传可能存在的误解。
• [bgwalter] 认为PyTorch代码库的表现不能作为可靠的基准，因为它并非由性能专家编写和优化，并指出AI生成方法仍然需要大量的人工指导和极端的引导。

补充讨论：
• [vessenes] 对方法论表示兴趣，特别是通过语言推理步骤来增加搜索的多样性，并认为这种方法似乎有效。
• [FL33TW00D] 在尝试复现时发现生成的LayerNorm内核在数值上不稳定，但之后问题得到了修正。
• [Workaccount2] 认为文章充满了兴奋的分享，但也希望有人能在发布前提出质疑，以确保结果的可靠性。
• [klingenm] 认为LLM在此更像是一个实现遗传算法的步骤，而非完全“AI生成”的独立成果。
• [yahoozoo] 对o3和Gemini 2.5 Pro的比较结果感兴趣，但遗憾于文章未说明哪个生成了更好的内核。
• [brrrrrm] 认为AI生成代码在处理大规模融合内核任务上将非常有趣，尤其是对人类来说繁琐的组合操作。
• [adityamwagh] 将LLM视为一种“集体智慧”，认为其能够完成复杂任务得益于训练数据中包含的大量人类思维过程。
• [MangoToupe] 对使用高端硬件如Nvidia L40S进行基准测试表示质疑，认为应使用消费者硬件以更贴近实际应用。
• [david-gpo] 基于过去的工作经验，怀疑AI生成的内核在某些特定参数下表现优于cuDNN选择的内核，可能是由于cuDNN在某些场景下选择了次优的内核，而非AI生成的内核真正超越了cuDNN。

争议焦点：AI生成内核是否真正超越了手动优化的内核，特别是PyTorch和cuDNN等高度优化的库。此外，关于AI生成方法是否需要过多的人工干预以及基准测试中使用高端硬件的合理性也存在讨论。

不同观点：

• [rwmj] 将乐器内部结构与船的甲板相比较，提供了视觉上的类比。

• [yard2010] 赞赏了照片的美感，同时批评了页面上的广告，形成了对比。
• [e40] 提到了对dpreview网站关闭的误解，并对网站的存续表示高兴。
• [gnabgib] 提到了之前类似的讨论和来源链接，提供了历史讨论的参考。
• [coreyp_1] 分享了自己购买过这些照片的经历，并表示可能会再次购买。
• [righthand] 幽默地提议拍摄手风琴或六角手风琴的内部照片，将讨论扩展到其他乐器。

data.title: Irritation Is Inspiration
data.author: j4mehta
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了 irritability（易怒或易烦躁）作为发现问题和创造机会的工具，特别是在创业和产品开发中。作者指出，许多让他感到烦躁的小问题，如糟糕的设计、拼写错误或低质量的产品，实际上是市场中的“ gaps”或未被解决的问题。这些 irritations 可以成为创业者的“超能力”，因为它们指向了需要改进的地方。文章强调，发现问题是创造新事物的关键，许多成功的产品和项目正是源于对现状的不满和解决这些问题的动力。作者通过自身经历说明， irritation 是灵感来源，鼓励大家不要忽视这种感受，而是利用它来推动创新和变革。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：个人在日常生活、技术使用和工作流程中遇到的烦恼和如何处理这些烦恼

不同观点：
• [chankstein38] 认为他的烦恼主要来源于无法控制的外部因素，比如产品质量问题和软件功能不合理。他还对AI生成内容的准确性表示怀疑，基于他与ChatGPT的互动经验，他不信任AI的输出结果，即使AI看起来能提供便利（如AI支持的播客）。

• [CommenterPerson] 对有人为解决回复邮件问题而开发软件感到不满，特别是当该软件还存在明显的错误（如讲稿中的错别字）。这反映出对开发质量和细节关注的批评。

• [pedalpete] 提出了一种更深层次的反思，认为人们常常被社会中根深蒂固的问题所困扰，但往往意识不到这些问题的存在。他通过自身长期失眠的经历，强调找到真正烦恼的根源并采取行动的重要性，建议通过探索他人如何处理类似问题来寻找解决方案。

• [PaulHou]le 分享了一个与技术细节有关的烦恼，提到有人对他儿子在模拟器上玩游戏的显示比例错误表示不满，以及他自己在演讲中犯的Excel图表错误。这体现出技术细节错误或不完美可能引发不满和争议。

• [hinkley] 提出了一种应对烦恼的策略，即把烦恼当作信息来处理。建议在遇到烦恼时停下来思考，是否能绕过问题而不是直接面对，或者找到一劳永逸的解决方案。

• [Daisywh] 提到微小的用户体验（UX）问题（如不关闭的下拉菜单）会让她感到烦恼，但她也意识到这些烦恼可以转化为有用的产品创意，并通过记录这些烦恼形成产品改进的思路。

• [esilverman] 提到了“怨恨驱动开发”（spite driven development）的概念，暗示有些开发行为可能是出于对某些问题的不满或怨恨而产生的。

• [bobrobpr] 表示对阅读Hacker News上“愚蠢的评论”感到厌烦，认为这是一个充满负面内容的平台，并对人性表示失望。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是对AI生成内容的信任问题。chankstein38基于个人经验对AI的可靠性提出质疑，而其他人可能认为AI能提供便利和创新机会。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是如何有效处理日常生活中的小烦恼，有人选择记录并转化为创意，有人建议通过反思和寻找替代方案来解决问题。
• pedalpete的反思提供了一种更深层次的解决问题的方法，即通过自我反思和探索他人的经验来找到真正有效的解决方案。

总的来说，评论中反映了人们对技术问题、产品质量和日常生活中的小烦恼的不同态度和处理方法。

44139286.article_content:
Be irritable
Your frustration is not a flaw. It’s a radar. And if you're a builder, it might just be your greatest asset.
Little things bother me.
Bad font choices. Typos. Weirdly aligned pixels. Push handles for pull doors. Pull handles for push doors. Low contrast photos. Apps that ask for notification access or a review without having delivered any value. Low quality packaging. A buggy app. Sloppy writing. A slow app. I can go on.
The fact that so many things bother me
also
used to bother me. But having spent enough time building my own products, I’ve come to realize something:
My irritation is my superpower.
Why?
Because these irritations are gaps.
They’re glitches in the Matrix — eye-opening,
if
we’re willing to take the red pill and look through them.
They’re problems — some small, some big. Some aren’t worth solving. Others are unsolvable.
But they’re problems.
And my job as an entrepreneur is to find problems and solve them.
It sounds simple in theory, but practically it’s very difficult.
Most people think that
solving
the problem is the hard part. And sure, that has its challenges.
But what happens if you don’t
spot
the problem in the first place?
If the way things are — the status quo — doesn’t strike you as problematic, then how do you ever build toward the future?
It reminds me of one of my favourite stories from
David Foster Wallace’s famous speech, This is Water
:
Two fish were casually swimming downstream in a river.
Eventually they come across another fish, who’s whistling and travelling upstream against the current.
As he swims by, he smiles and says: “How’s the water, boys!” and continues past them.
A few moments pass. The two fish keep swimming in silence.
Eventually, one of them looks at the other and says:
“What the hell is water?
As a creator, builder, or thinker — if you accept reality as-is, it'll become impossible to create something new.
Irritation is your way out.
If something irritates you or surprises you, it likely represents an opportunity.
An opportunity to solve. To build. To create. To publish. To invent.
This has played out so many times in my own life:
It irritated me that I didn’t know enough about Indian history, despite those being my roots. All the existing podcasts were built for an Indian audience — none catered to Western second-generation immigrants. So I created an AI-powered podcast called
The Other Side
that does exactly this.
It irritated me that I had to manually reply to 20+ emails every day from reporters just to get some press for my startup. So I built
a software
to do it for me.
It irritated me that AI research was moving so fast, and my job relied on staying on top of it — but I had no system. So I built
a platform
to filter and curate new papers.
And the list goes on…
My current startup,
Swift
only exists because an irritated sports facility owner came to us, looking for help.
Irritation is inspiration.
Don’t let it go.

data.title: Jerry Lewis's "The Day the Clown Cried" discovered in Sweden after 53 years
data.author: danso
data.article_summary: 喜剧演员杰瑞·刘易斯（Jerry Lewis）1972年拍摄的争议性电影《The Day the Clown Cried》因未公开发行而被视为“遗失影片”。该片讲述了一名德国马戏团小丑因 mocking 希特勒被关入纳粹集中营，并被迫诱骗儿童走向死亡的故事。多年以来，人们认为该片没有完整版本存在。然而，瑞典演员Hans Crispin近日透露，他于1980年从制作公司的档案中秘密取走了一份完整的影片工作拷贝，并一直私下放映。Crispin表示他打算将此拷贝交给下一代，并希望通过修复使其公开。尽管刘易斯曾于2015年将部分影片素材捐赠给美国国会图书馆，并规定2024年6月前不得公开，但完整影片至今未见天日。Crispin的发现引发了关于该片是否应公之于众的讨论。

44139592.article_content:
One of cinema's most sought-after
lost films
has been discovered after having been kept secretly in the collection of a Swedish actor for 45 years.
Comedian
Jerry Lewis
's controversial holocaust film
The Day the Clown Cried,
shot in 1972 but never released, was thought to
not exist in finished form
.
But Hans Crispin, star of the beloved 1980s Swedish TV series
Angne & Svullo
, claims he stole a complete workprint of the film from the archives of its production studio in 1980 – and has been screening it for guests in his apartment ever since.
“I have the only copy,” Crispin told
Swedish state news broadcaster SVT.
“I stole it from Europafilm in 1980 and copied it to VHS in the attic where we copied other films at night.
“I've kept the copy in my bank vault,” Crispin added.
Swedish actor Hans Crispin has a complete workprint of The Day The Clown Cried, SVT has reported. AFP
Crispin recently screened a full copy to journalists from SVT and Sweden's
Icon
magazine to prove his claim was true.
“You're the 23rd and 24th people I've shown it to,” he told
Icon
and SVT.
The actor also revealed that his initial copy was missing the opening six-minute sequence of the film shot in Paris, which was mailed to him anonymously in 1990, along with a note saying that the sender knew he possessed a copy of the rest of the film.
Will The Day The Clown Cried be released to the public?
Now that he has come out into the open, Crispin intends to make his copy available for the world to see, saying: “It must be seen!”
Crispin added: “I think I want to hand it over to the next generation. With today's technique, it can be restored. I want to sell it to a serious producer who either restores it or keeps it locked away, or restores it and shows it to people for studying purposes.”
The film tells the story of a German circus clown who is imprisoned in a Nazi concentration camp for mocking
Adolf Hitler
and is then forced to lure children to their deaths as punishment.
The footage that Lewis possessed of the Day The Clown Cried was donated to the Library of Congress in 2015. AFP
Lewis, who directed and starred in the film as clown Helmut Doork, donated five hours of footage to the US Library of Congress in 2015, adding a stipulation that it not be made available until June 2024.
The footage, which has been made available to scholars, was screened last August for
The New Republic
journalist Benjamin Charles Germain Lee, who reported that the footage was fragmentary and does not constitute a complete film, leading the industry to conclude that the full film did not exist.
Why the film was never released
While there were myriad alleged issues during the shoot itself, problems reportedly arose between Lewis and producer Nat Wachsberger once filming stopped, which is considered the main catalyst for the film's shelving.
Lewis was reportedly unsatisfied with the film’s financing and announced that Wachsberger did not fulfil his financial obligations. Hearing this, Wachsberger threatened to sue Lewis for breach of contract, which resulted in a fallout between the two that caused Lewis to leave with a rough cut of the film, according to a 2018 feature in
The New York Times.
Lewis had mixed feelings about the film, showing fragments of his footage to close friends. However, in his 1982 autobiography, Lewis said “the picture must be seen”.
No complete copy of The Day The Clown Cried has ever been confirmed to exist until now. AFP
After watching it,
The Simpsons
voice actor Harry Shearer said it was “a perfect object”, adding: “This movie is so drastically wrong, its pathos and its comedy are so wildly misplaced, that you could not, in your fantasy of what it might be like, improve on what it really is.”
In an interview with
The New York Times
in 2018, Chris Lewis, the comedian's son, said: “It was something that was very close to his heart.”
At other times, however, Lewis denounced the film. In 2013, footage of him surfaced on YouTube in which he stated: “It was bad, and it was bad because I lost the magic. No one will ever see it, because I'm embarrassed at the poor work.”
The history of lost films
The Day the Crown Cried
is an example of one of many films that were once thought lost or not fit for public screening.
Similar films include 1976’s
Chess of the Wind
by Iranian director
Mohammad Reza Aslani.
Until it was rediscovered in 2020, the film could only be watched on low-quality VHS tapes. Since then, it has been restored and screened around the world.
One of the best-known lost films is
The Passion of Joan of Arc
from 1928. After being lost for years, a copy was found in a Norwegian hospital in the 1980s. The film is now considered one of the most important historical film artefacts.
The Day The Clown Cried depicts a clown entertaining children during the holocaust. AFP
London After Midnight
, a 1927 horror film directed by Tod Browning starring Lon Chaney, is still a veritable white whale for fans after the last-known copy was destroyed in

data.title: Show HN: Asdf Overlay – High performance in-game overlay library for Windows
data.author: storycraft
data.article_summary: Asdf Overlay 是一个高性能、易于使用的 Windows 游戏叠加库，支持多种渲染 API（如 OpenGL、DirectX 和 Vulkan），通过 GPU 共享纹理实现加速，避免了 CPU 上的帧缓冲复制，从而在任意大小下保持高效渲染。它支持多后端、输入捕获控制，并提供示例项目如游戏内浏览器和噪声矩形。该项目使用 Rust 开发，需要 node 和 pnpm 进行构建，并提供了详细的构建和运行说明。Asdf Overlay 采用双重许可：MIT 或 Apache-2.0。

Icepi Zero - The portable FPGA development board.
What is the Icepi Zero?
Icepi Zero is an economical FPGA development board with a Raspberry Pi Zero form factor. It carries a Lattice ECP5 25F, enabling powerful designs while keeping a small portable size. It also has a HDM- port allowing easy digital video output.
View PCB online
Why Icepi Zero?
Currently most powerful FPGA boards on the market are expensive and bulky.
I've always wanted a low-cost portable FPGA with video output to make my own CPU, but there isn't any on the market.
The Icepi Zero aims to fix this. Carrying a powerful ECP5 FPGA on a small Raspberry Pi Zero form factor, it is the ultimate portable solution for FPGA development. Additionally packing a HDM- mini port and 3 USB-C ports, it allows interfacing with multiple external I/O devices.
Icepi Zero is for everyone: Students can use it to learn about the internals of modern processors. Gamers can use it to emulate old hardware. Programmers can use it to test their code on multiple architecture.
Icepi Zero also has an on-board USB to JTAG converter, so no external programmers are needed. Moreover Icepi Zero is fully open-source, no strings attached. Fabricate your own boards if you want one!
Features
Raspberry Pi Zero form factor
Lattice ECP5U FPGA:
24k LUT
112 KiB of RAM
One MiniGPDI connector (it's HDM- but I don't have the money to buy a license...)
Three USB-C Ports
256Mbit 166MHz SDRAM
MicroSD card slot
On-board USB to JTAG and UART converter
40MHz external oscillator
128 Mbit of flash
4 user LEDs
1 user button
This powerful configuration allows the PCB to be used in numerous ways, including real time video processing, hardware AI acceleration and prototyping of ASICs.
Usage
Check out the
firmware
folder for example code and compilation instructions!
If you want to order this board, it uses a 1.2mm PCB with JLC04121H-7628 Stackup. Gerbers are in the
production
folder in the
hardware
directory.

data.title: How to run cron jobs in Postgres without extra infrastructure
data.author: Liriel
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了如何使用Wasp和PgBoss实现轻量级任务调度。PgBoss是一个基于PostgreSQL的作业队列系统，利用数据库的可靠性和扩展性来高效管理后台任务，无需额外基础设施。Wasp是一个全栈框架，简化了与PgBoss的集成，提供声明式任务定义、自动配置以及类型安全等优点。对于大多数小型项目和早期创业公司，这种组合足够处理每日低于1000个任务的场景，尤其是简单的任务如发送提醒邮件。但如果任务耗时长、数量多或涉及复杂计算，则应考虑使用独立的任务处理系统。文章还通过一个网球比分跟踪应用示例演示了如何创建一次性调度任务和周期性CRON任务。基本要求包括Node.js、PostgreSQL、Google OAuth认证和Mailgun配置。

不同观点：
• NeutralForest认为systemd timers比cron更易用，尤其是在RHEL环境中。他提到systemd的定时器接口在管理和列出任务方面更友好，并且可以像管理服务一样管理定时任务。
• zie列举了多个与PostgreSQL相关的任务调度和队列工具，如pg_boss、bq、pg_timetable等，认为选择很多，没有必要局限于某一个工具。

44114436.article_content:
I had the pleasure to spend nearly 3 years working on live video infrastructure at TV2 Norway. As you know, when it comes to infrastructure, time
IS
money. Everything needs to be just-in-time, especially when it comes to provisioning costly components like encoders. For example, if there's a major live sports match scheduled, you want to ensure the streaming infrastructure is set up just minutes before kickoff, and torn down shortly after the final whistle blows.
The fact is, scheduling is synonymous with infrastructure complexity. But sometimes you're just working on your trusty little Node app, and all you really need is something simple — like sending a daily reminder to users about today's coding challenge. That's exactly the kind of lightweight scheduling we'll dive into in this article.
Scheduling Jobs with Wasp and PgBoss
​
What is PgBoss?
​
PgBoss
is a job queue built on
PostgreSQL
. It leverages the database's reliability, transactional safety, and scalability to manage background jobs efficiently. Unlike Redis-based queues, PgBoss doesn't require additional infrastructure — just Postgres, which is a great fit if you're already using it as your database.
Key features:
Transactional safety
– jobs are stored in Postgres, ensuring they survive crashes.
Retries & timeouts
– failed jobs can be automatically retried.
Scheduling
– supports both delayed and recurring (CRON) jobs.
No extra infrastructure
- only Postgres needed.
Why Wasp Makes It Even Better
​
Wasp
is a full-stack framework for React & Node.js that simplifies web app development by handling boilerplate for you. When combined with PgBoss, Wasp provides:
Declarative job definitions
– define jobs directly in your Wasp config.
Everything just works
– no need to manually set up workers or queues.
Type safety
– jobs are type-checked, reducing runtime errors.
NOTE: Since PgBoss runs in the same process as your Wasp app, CPU-heavy jobs can impact API responsiveness. For high-load scenarios, consider offloading to a dedicated worker process.
When Should You Consider a Different Solution?
For most side projects and early-stage startups, this setup will work perfectly fine. As a rule of thumb, if you're processing less than 1000 jobs per day or your jobs are mostly lightweight operations (like sending emails or updating records), you can stick with this solution.
However, you might want to consider a dedicated job processing system when:
Your jobs take more than a few seconds to complete.
You're processing thousands of jobs per day.
Your jobs involve heavy computational tasks (like image processing or data analysis).
You need to scale job processing independently from your main application
A dedicated system means running your jobs on a separate server or process, isolated from your main application. This prevents long-running jobs from affecting your app's performance.
But remember: premature optimization is the root of all evil. Start with this simple solution, and only upgrade when you have concrete evidence that you need something more robust.
We'll look at two use cases:
One-time scheduled jobs (e.g., send a reminder email at a specific time).
Recurring  (CRON) jobs (e.g., daily digest emails).
We are going to use the
Wasp Tennis Score
example app to demonstrate the functionality.
The main interface of our tennis score tracking app
This is a neat little tennis score tracking app we've built. Think of it like this: you're running a tennis tournament and need to keep track of who's winning. The judges can punch in scores as the matches happen, and everyone watching can see the results.
To run the app, you'll need to clone the repo, create a new
.env.server
file (copy
example.env.server
as a starting point), populate it with the required values and execute the sequence of commands listed in the
README file here.
Requirements:
Node.js
≥20 installed — I recommend using
nvm
.
A
Postgres
database connection URL — but in our case for development you can just use
wasp db start
.
Google OAuth
credentials (Client ID and Client Secret)
Mailgun
config (API Key, Domain, API Url)
How to Create Scheduled Jobs with Wasp
​
After cloning the repository, you can check out the working example implementation of the scheduled job feature by running the following command:
git
checkout scheduled_job_added
Start the app with
wasp start
and authenticate with Google.
You'll be met with a UI that displays a list of tennis matches. Ongoing (i.e. Live) matches on the top and Completed Matches below.
In the header you will find a "Schedule Summary Email" button. That button is configured to send you a summary of the previous day's matches to your email.
The logged-in interface of our tennis scoring app
Click the button and check the email address linked to your Google account. You should see something similar to the screenshot below.
Email summary screenshot
Since this is a new account without any record of previous day's matches, the summary will be empty.

• verdverm推荐使用PG-Boss，并分享了自己用其设置刷新认证令牌任务的经验。虽然文档较少，但使用简单。同时对WASP及其自定义DSL持否定态度。
• mitjam提到Kubernetes CronJobs是一个不错的选择，特别是在已经使用Kubernetes的环境中，无需额外基础设施。
• xnx对文章未提及pg_cron表示疑问。
• lukasb提到自己是Next.js和neon用户，暗示可能有不同的需求或视角。
• wewewedxfgdf认为有多种方法可以解决任务调度问题，个人专注于systemd timers，但也承认其他人可能有不同的有效方法。
• mati365质疑文章是否完全由AI编写，对其质量表示怀疑。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是不同工具的选择和评价，用户根据自己的经验和需求推荐不同的工具。
• 另一个值得注意的点是系统级任务调度工具（如cron和systemd）与应用级任务队列工具之间的比较，用户在讨论中提出了各自的优缺点。
• 对PG-Boss的评价较为正面，但对其文档和抽象持保留意见。
• 对文章质量的质疑虽然存在，但未成为主要讨论点。

data.author: tanelpoder
data.article_summary: CatBench是一款使用Postgres和PgVector的演示应用，利用Kaggle上的25k张宠物照片展示相似性搜索功能如何与应用代码及数据库模式（HammerDB Order Entry）结合使用。通过其交互式界面，用户可以点击猫的照片，获取基于相似外观猫的购买推荐。该应用将向量搜索结果与常规应用模式结合，并显示后台SQL查询及其执行计划指标。最新版本v0.3增加了压力测试和Postgres实例级活动及SQL延迟指标图表，并有一个“监控”按钮展示查询性能。未来计划包括扩展至9百万张照片，增加召回质量监控，并支持其他数据库。CatBench旨在作为学习工具，帮助用户理解向量相似性搜索工作负载及查询执行情况。

不同观点：

• 争议的焦点在于该项目是否可以被视为一个真正的基准测试工具，以及其命名是否准确传达了其功能和用途。

44139382.article_content:
CatBench is a Postgres + PgVector demo application that uses 25k pet photos from a Kaggle dataset for demonstrating how the similarity search features work together with the rest of your application code & schema in the backend (HammerDB Order Entry).
CatBench Interactive UI
You can navigate around the
recommendation engine for Cat Purchases
UI, click on cat photos and find product recommendations, based on what other similar-looking cats have purchased. This is where CatBench
joins vector search results together with your regular application schema
. When you scroll down, you see the backend SQL queries of your UI activity with their plan execution metrics (see below):
The app ran every backend query twice, first with
EXPLAIN (ANZLYZE, BUFFERS)
, so that you’d see how many physical block I/Os these queries do - and the second run was to retrieve data to display in the UI.
This gives you a nice sample of what your UI queries are waiting for, how many buffers they visit and how many rows they pass around the plan (including number of loops & revisits through some parts of your plan).
New in CatBench v0.3: Stress-test + Postgres instance-wide activity & SQL latency metrics
The latest version of
CatBench
has Postgres instance-wide
throughput
and average query execution
latency charts
built in. Now there’s a new button “Monitoring” on the CatBench landing page. I usually open it in a new tab while navigating around the rest of the app.
Here’s a screenshot from a test where I gradually increased the number of cat & dog similarity search query loops from 4 to 16 on a freshly restarted Postgres instance (and the OS pagecache had been cleared too):
More new stuff in the latest version
In addition to the query performance charts, it shows top queries in a tabular format too:
I moved a couple of charts into the bottom as they aren’t that useful/great yet, the Buffer Activity one is problematic as I use PL/PgSQL loops for running lots of concurrent similarity searches, but at least in my default configuration, the Buffer Activity metrics are not updated during the PL/PgSQL loop, so you don’t see much activity there, until the whole loop finishes (and then you get a huge spike that covers all the 10+ minutes of its runtime). More tweaking is needed.
Future plans
Other than tweaking/bugfixing, this is where I plan to go:
Tidy up the code and install instructions for “exploding” the 25k photos to
9 million photos
, by creating additional 359 copies of each photo (each rotated by one more degree). This also enables the next step:
Add a
recall
quality monitoring for the “cat fraud detection” reverse lookup queries - this allows us to start playing with different vector index types and build configuration settings and have nice performance
and
recall quality charts to compare.
Refactor the whole thing to
support other databases
too, not really for any competitive benchmarking reasons, but for additional learning and fun!
Check it out and leave feedback here:
CatBench GitHub
Have fun! :-)
Notes
The whole app is meant to be a learning tool, an easy way to run some vector similariy search workloads (together with other application data)
and
be able to see the various query texts, execution plans and plan execution metrics when you navigate around. Currently you’d need to adjust/rebuild your database settings and vector index parameters manually, to compare how well some vector index type or setting works for you. I will automate some of these things in the future.
A previous announcement article with some more reasoning about what and why I’m building is here:
CatBench Vector Search Playground

data.title: Ray Tracing in J
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了作者使用J语言编写的一个简易光线追踪器。J语言以其简洁和独特的ASCII语法而闻名，虽然初学者可能觉得其语法晦涩，但理解其数组编程范式后会发现语法并非主要障碍。文章重点解释了J语言中的隐式函数（tacit verbs），特别是三动词组合的fork结构，如计算平均数的例子。此外，还讨论了J语言中从右到左的计算顺序。

作者定义了一些实用函数，如计算向量长度的`magnitude`，以及向量归一化的`normalize`和点积的`dotproduct`。为了处理颜色，作者定义了将值限制在0到255之间的`toRGB`。文章还介绍了函数组合和部分应用的技巧，如使用`&`进行参数部分应用。最后，定义了反射函数`reflect`和选择最小正交交点的`hit`函数，用于确定光线与球体的首次接触点。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：J语言在几何计算中的应用及其与其他编程范式的对比

不同观点：
• Vox_Leone认为J语言在数组处理和几何计算方面非常强大，但提出可以结合更高层次的语义框架（如其Python项目SpinStep）来进行基于方向的树结构遍历，以补充J语言的低层次计算能力。Vox_Leone强调了结合不同编程范式以实现更复杂的定向推理的可能性。
• gcanyon对文章中未提及的J语言的其他重要特性进行了补充，如 tacit syntax、Hook和"under" conjunction。他指出J语言可以通过复杂的verb组合实现强大的功能，并提供了更简洁的向量长度计算方法。gcanyon的评论更侧重于J语言的内部机制和语法特性。
• magicalhippo对文章没有重新实现SmallPT表示失望，认为如果能够处理多种不同对象、不同材质以及递归等特性会更有趣。这表明他期望看到更复杂和多功能的实现。

补充讨论：
• bobsmooth的评论并未直接参与关于J语言或SmallPT的讨论，而是提出一个技术社区中常见问题的幽默建议，即统计某类问题在Hacker News上被发布的次数。这属于对社区讨论内容的元讨论，而非直接的技术分析。

争议焦点：
• 主要争议在于对文章内容深度的期望不同。Vox_Leone和magicalhippo对文章内容的期望超出了文章实际讨论的范围，前者关注更高层次的框架结合，后者则希望看到更复杂的实现。而gcanyon则专注于补充文章中未详述的J语言特性。

44118646.article_content:
Ray Tracing in J
2020-04-18
I've been reading up on J and decided another small project was in
order, this time I've written a minimal ray tracer.
Brevity
J is, perhaps infamously, a terse language. I think it may sometimes
get unfairly discounted for this brevity because of the flavor of the
syntax (namely, ASCII). It can be a little hard to describe, but the
syntax isn't the hard part of learning J, the jarring parts are a
result of the paradigm differences in array programming. By the time
I've started to wrap my head around the very functional, array
oriented style of programming the syntax has started to fall away. At
least in the case of my own code I don't find the syntax being an
obstacle, I'm curious how this would hold up in the face of someone
else's code.
Tacit Verbs
One piece of syntax that bears explaining is J's means of tacit
programming (that is, functions which make no reference to their
arguments). While there is a bit more depth to it than I bother using,
I've limited myself to using mostly trains of three verbs, so-called
forks
. A fork is a function comprised of three verbs, F G and H and
might look like this:
myNewVerb=. F G H    NB. results in application (F(y)) G (H(y))
The parsing rules for J identify this pattern and apply the function
in a specific way; the canonical example is to define "average":
sum=. +/
divide=. %
count=. #
average=. sum divide count
If you applied it to an array
1 2 3 4 5
:
average 1 2 3 4 5
NB. (sum 1 2 3 4 5) divide (count 1 2 3 4 5)
One last thing that may confuse the untrained eye is the order of
evaluation. Sentences respect the traditional means of evaluating
parenthesized phrases first, but otherwise proceed from right to
left. An example:
- +/ 1 2 3
_6
The result will be the sum of
1 2 3
(6), which is then negated, so
the result is -6 (which is written as
_6
to avoid confusion with the
minus/negate symbol).
Utility Verbs
I've written several verbs in the tacit style that are generally
useful or improve the reading of the program, even when they're only
used once. The first is
magnitude
, which returns the magnitude of a
vector:
magnitude=: [: %: [: +/ *:      NB. sqrt of sum of squares
The comment should suffice for those who don't yet know the syntax of
J but it may be worth pointing out two interesting details. The first
is the fact that this "train" looks like it is 5 verbs, which doesn't
sound like a
fork
at first. The thing to keep in mind is that forks
can compose on top of other forks, so this may be viewed like:
[: %: [: +/ *:
a train of 5 verbs
[: %: ([: +/ *:)
the first fork is parenthesized
the second fork is now F G H, where H is the parenthesized fork
the resulting application is like
([: y) %: (([: +/ *:) y)
The use of
[:
is a little weird to understand, but it is basically a
no-operation left argument to ensure that the verb is evaluated as a
function of one argument instead of two. This is a consequence of J's
overloading of verbs for the two cases, e.g.
3 % 4
is "3 divided by
4", but
% 4
is "reciprocal of 4". By using
[:
in a train we ensure
that whatever is left of
%
isn't taken as a left argument and
instead we use the monadic form of the verb.
Although it isn't used much here, one thing that is really attractive
about array programming is the way verbs can operate independent of
dimensionality. Here I take the magnitude of a two-dimensional vector
and then a three-dimensional vector (which is what I use throughout
the ray tracer):
magnitude 6 8
10
magnitude 3 4 12
13
normalize=: ] * [: % magnitude  NB. scale by reciprocal of magnitude
dotproduct=: +/ . *
Both normalize and dot product aren't particularly interesting,
normalize is notable for composing a new verb train from the
previously defined
magnitude
without any special syntax or handling.
toRGB=: ([: <.&255 >.&0) & ([: <. 255&*) NB. 0->1 becomes 0->255 (clamped)
Throughout the ray tracer I deal with color as vectors of 3 floating
point numbers, intended to be between 0 and 1.0. In order to map the
range into the RGB space I'm doing
max(0, min(floor(x * 255),
255))
.
&
("bond") is used to partially apply arguments to a verb, a
simple example would be to define "addOne" as
+&1
. Interestingly,
&
can bond nouns to verbs to apply arguments but it may also be used
to compose functions as in math, e.g.
(f â g)(x) = f(g(x))
is
analogous to
f&g y
(eliding
a few
details
here).
Reflection is defined as a verb taking two argument, a vector and a
normal. It works by subtracting the vector and the normal scaled by
twice the dot product of the vector and the normal.
reflect=: [ - ] * +:@dotproduct          NB. (vector normal)
Given an array of intersections (defined later) a "hit" is defined as
the smallest positive intersection. This identifies which of the
points the ray "touches" are to be drawn, since the vector "moves" in
the time dimension it means we pick the first contact of the ray with
the sphere:
hit=: ([: {. /:~) & (0&< # ])   NB. smallest positive intersection

data.title: Colour and Shape: Using Computer Vision to Explore the Science Museum (2020)
data.author: airstrike
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了通过对科学博物馆集团藏品的7000多张物品照片进行计算机视觉分析，探索物品的形状、颜色和纹理。研究聚焦于21个类别的日常物品，如摄影技术、计时器和家用电器等。分析显示，最常见的颜色为深炭灰色，且随着时间推移，物品颜色从棕色和黄色逐渐向灰色转变，可能与材料从木材向塑料转变有关。此外，研究还对比了旧技术（如1844年的电报）与新技术（如iPhone 3G）的颜色差异，发现旧物品颜色更为多样。该研究不仅丰富了博物馆的目录信息，还提供了新的在线藏品检索方式。

44138879.article_content:
Colour & Shape: Using Computer Vision to Explore the Science Museum Group Collection
Cath Sleeman
Follow
11 min read
·
Oct 8, 2020
--
3
Listen
Share
Introduction
Online museum collections provide a treasure trove of objects to explore. They also allow visitors to view a much larger proportion of a museum’s collection than they could see by visiting the museum in person; the majority of many museum collections are kept in storage.
This article analyses a selection of the
Science Museum Group Collection
. We examined over 7,000 photographs of objects from 21 categories. The categories were selected on the basis that they contained large numbers of everyday or familiar objects. These categories range from photographic technology to time measurement, lighting to printing and writing, and domestic appliances to navigation.¹
The photographs allow us to study the form of objects — their shape, colour and texture. The insights gleaned can be used to enrich a museum’s catalogue and expand the ways of searching through the online collection. More broadly, this analysis shows how a photographic dataset can shed new light on a museum’s collection.
This research was funded by the
Creative Industries Policy and Evidence Centre (PEC)
.
All the orange hues within the objects that we analysed.
Colour
The most common
Amongst the 7,083 objects that we analysed, the most common colour was a dark charcoal grey. The collage below shows objects that contain large amounts of this colour. While this grey appears in over 80% of the photographs that we studied, in most cases it only makes up a tiny fraction of the pixels in any one photograph.
A selection of objects that contain large amounts of the most common colour (a dark charcoal grey).
Changes in colour over time
Changes in the colour of objects over time.
The image on the left shows how the colours of objects have changed over time. Each object was assigned to a year group (spanning 20 years), based on the earliest year associated with the object. We then calculated the mix of colours amongst the objects in each group.
The video below provides a more detailed picture of how colour has evolved. The objects are ordered by their earliest date and each frame shows the mix of colours in overlapping groups of objects.
Each frame shows the 2,000 most common colours amongst a group of 250 objects. One example of an object from that group is also shown. The groups of objects overlap; 10 new objects are introduced and removed with each subsequent frame.
The most notable trend, in both the chart and the video, is the rise in grey over time. This is matched by a decline in brown and yellow. These trends likely reflect changes in materials, such as the move away from wood and towards plastic. A smaller trend is the use of very saturated colours which begins in the 1960s.
While things appear to have become a little greyer over time, we must remember that the photographs examined here are a just a sample of the objects within the collection, and the collection itself is also a non-random selection of objects. Moreover, these trends will continue to change as new objects are acquired.
All the yellow hues within the objects that we analysed.
The colours within a single object
The video below illustrates the huge array of colours that can be found within a single object. The object in question is a
Century Model 46 plate camera
, dating from 1900. It can be found in The Kodak Collection at the National Science and Media Museum in Bradford.
All the colours in a Century Model 46 plate camera.
Colours in old and new technology
The images below contrast the range of colours in a
telegraph
from 1844 with an
iPhone 3G mobile phone
from 2008–2010. The telegraph is a Cooke and Wheatstone double needle telegraph which relays messages by using needles that point to different letters on the dial.
Comparing the colours in old and new technology.
The wide range of colours in the telegraph comes in large part from the mahogany wood used in its construction. But the colours also come from its shape (the rounded pillars reflect light and create shadows) as well as its age (the wear and tear creates colour variations). In contrast, the metal and plastic materials in the iPhone give much less variation. It also has a more basic shape and is in better condition.

The dataset of photographs can also be used to identify tiny amounts of colour across large numbers of objects. Using Google products in 2025 means using (or avoiding) AI features, which are becoming a core part of the experience across the board. Last year, Gmail gained the ability to
summarize emails
on demand. Now, Google says AI summaries will be generated and displayed automatically in the Gmail app for Android and iOS.
Before this latest change, you had to tap the "Summarize this email" chip at the top of the screen to generate an AI summary of the message contents.
Google has decided
to make this automatic for emails "where a summary is helpful." That means messages that are longer or threads that contain multiple replies. The announcement is a bit vague about how much detail will trigger a summary, but it probably won't take much, as Google wants people interacting with AI features as much as possible.
Gmail's AI summaries use Gemini to generate a brief list of bullet points that break down the content of the thread. It appears at the top of the app, which may not be ideal. In the same way that AI Overviews appear at the top of search results and
push the actual search results farther out of reach
, Gmail's AI summaries take up valuable real estate at the top of the screen.
The summaries will appear automatically for English-language emails, but it may take up to 15 days for this change to roll out to everyone. The automatic summaries will appear for all paid Workspace accounts, as well as individual accounts with Google AI Premium subscriptions. It's unclear whether standard Gmail accounts will get the expanded summaries, but the move appears to be a step toward making summaries the default for everyone. Likewise, Google could easily expand the use of summaries in the web version of Gmail at any time.
This block of AI-generated text will soon appear automatically in some threads.
Credit:
Google
This block of AI-generated text will soon appear automatically in some threads.
Credit:
Google
Summarizing content is one of the more judicious applications of generative AI technology, dating back to the 2017 paper on the transformer architecture. Generative AI has since been employed to create chatbots that will seemingly answer any question, despite their tendency to make mistakes. Grounding the AI output with a few emails usually yields accurate results, but do you really need a robot to summarize your emails? Unless you're getting novels in your inbox, you can probably just read a few paragraphs.
If you're certain you don't want any part of this, there is a solution. Automatic generation of AI summaries is controlled by Gmail's "smart features." You (or an administrator of your managed account) can
disable that
. Open the app settings, select the account, and uncheck the smart features toggle.
For most people, Gmail's smart features are enabled out of the box, but they're off by default in Europe and Japan. When you disable them, you won't see the automatic AI summaries, but there will still be a button to generate those summaries with Gemini. Be aware that smart features also control high-priority notifications, package tracking,
Smart Compose
,
Smart Reply
, and
nudges
. If you can live without all of those features in the mobile app, you can avoid automatic AI summaries. The app will occasionally pester you to turn smart features back on, though.

data.article_summary: Fractran是一种由数学家约翰·康威发明的图灵完备的深奥编程语言。一个Fractran程序由一组有序的正分数构成，并需要一个初始正整数输入n。程序运行规则如下：找出列表中第一个使n乘以该分数后结果为整数的fraction f，将n更新为n乘以f的值，重复此过程直到找不到符合条件的分数，程序停止。该链接提供了Fractran解释器的源代码和示例，展示了如何生成质数序列等功能。

主要讨论点：Fractran语言的编程可行性及其实用工具开发

不同观点：
• 观点一：Fractran是一种看似无法编程的深奥语言，但通过系统地跟踪示例，可以发现其编程潜力。支持该观点的用户siraben表示，虽然Fractran一开始看起来无法编写程序，但通过示例逐步解析，可以理解其工作原理。

补充讨论：
• 示例展示：siraben提供了一个具体的Fractran程序示例，展示了如何用汇编风格编写和优化一个计算1到10累加的程序。该示例包括程序代码和运行结果，展示了工具的实际应用效果。

通过这些观点和示例，可以看出Fractran虽然复杂且难以直接编程，但通过系统化的分析和工具支持，仍然可以有效地用于编程任务。

What is Fractran?
From wikipedia
Fractran
:
FRACTRAN is a Turing-complete esoteric programming language invented by the mathematician John Conway. A FRACTRAN program is an ordered list of positive fractions together with an initial positive integer input n. The program is run by updating the integer n as follows:
for the first fraction f in the list for which nf is an integer, replace n by nf
repeat this rule until no fraction in the list produces an integer when multiplied by n, then halt.

data.title: Use AI code tools as collaborators, not crutches
data.author: adityaoberai1
data.article_summary: 文章主要批评了当前过度依赖“氛围编码”（vibe coding）的趋势，即开发者在不理解技术细节的情况下，依赖AI工具生成代码，导致安全和质量问题。作者强调，尽管AI工具可以帮助加速开发，但开发者仍需掌握基础知识，如系统架构、数据处理和安全实践。文章提出三点建议：首先，开发者应学习并理解自己正在构建的内容，避免盲目生成代码；其次，在编码前应暂停思考，评估最佳方案；最后，应在编码前做好规划，确保代码逻辑清晰。作者警告，忽视这些基础而依赖“氛围编码”可能导致严重后果，开发者必须对自己的代码负责。

Do You Control The Tools Or Do The Tools Control You?

These days, the hype around vibe coding feels limitless. Tools that promise to turn your ideas into apps with nothing more than a chat prompt are everywhere. But back in March this year, I came across a tweet from a developer who discovered that one of those tools, Lovable, was exposing a user's Supabase API key. While it was a publishable API key, it had no permissions or restrictions, and the developer was able to access all the app's data without authentication, just by looking at the public build.
This is not innovation. This is a security breach waiting to happen.
This is what happens when people lean too hard on the vibe. They build software by instinct, skip fundamentals, and trust that the tool knows best. But when you are shipping products that handle real data, real users, and real consequences, vibes alone will not cut it.
Welcome to 2025, where AI code-generation tools can get you 80 percent of the way there. And yet,
so many early-career developers are building software like they are writing poetry at an open mic
. No structure, no planning, no understanding. Just vibes. It’s high time we start fixing that!
Are Vibe Coding And AI-Assisted Coding The Same Thing?
First, let’s clear the air. Vibe coding is not the same as using an AI assistant.
Vibe coding
is what happens when you build software without understanding how anything works
, relying entirely on tools to fill in the gaps. You feed ChatGPT a vague prompt, drag in some randomly generated code blocks, wire up a few buttons, and hope it works. You ship without testing. You copy code you don’t understand. You build with vibes, not logic.
AI-assisted coding
, on the other hand,
is intentional.
You still plan your features. You still understand how your system fits together. You just move faster because you’ve got an AI pair programmer who helps with boilerplate, explains confusing concepts, and suggests things you were going to write anyway.
The difference is in the mindset.
AI-assisted developers are still the architects, while vibe coders hope the house stands because someone else drew the blueprint.
The Basics Still Matter
Even with AI, you still need to be a developer. If you’re not doing these things, please start today!
#1: Learn What You’re Building
Wanting to skip the learning process before building is the number one reason for the sloppily generated code currently available. It is precisely how developers lose all control over what they are building.
If you’re building an authentication system, you can’t not learn what tokens are, how sessions work, and why storing passwords in plaintext is a terrible idea. If you’re calling APIs, you must understand how requests are structured, what status codes mean, and how to handle errors gracefully. If you’re storing data, you should know how relational and NoSQL databases differ, when to use indexes, and what trade-offs come with each schema decision.
AI can help you write the code, but it can’t teach you to care.
That part is on you.  And in this case, to care is also to control. Every decision you delegate without understanding becomes a potential landmine waiting to explode (maybe not today, but definitely someday!)
#2: Pause and Assess
Before you open Cursor, start wiring up a UI, or churning out an API, just pause and ask yourself:
What am I actually trying to build?
Can I describe the core flow of this feature out loud or on paper?
Is there a simpler solution hiding behind the flashy one?
Every minute spent thinking before you build will save you ten debugging later. That pause could be the difference between launching a feature that works and shipping one that silently breaks user data in production.
Sometimes, the best code is no code
(or just a well-placed conditional). But you won’t realize that if you rush to prompt before you plan.
#3: Plan Before You Code
Design still matters, now more than ever. Start outlining your features, sketching out your user journeys, and writing pseudocode if that helps you structure your logic.
Even a basic plan, a few bullets on what the function needs to do, can guide your AI assistant to better output. If you just prompt
“build me an upload feature”,
the results will vary wildly. But if you’ve already planned:
“I need to let users upload PDF files up to 10MB, store them in an S3 storage bucket, and tag them by user ID”
, now you’ve got a little more clarity than before (and you still need more but hey, it’s a start).
Think about how data flows through your app, how users interact with it, and where things might break. These are the habits that turn junior developers into senior on

data.article_summary: E2 SSDs是旨在填补高容量存储市场空缺的新型固态硬盘，单驱动器容量可达1PB，介于传统HDD和高效能SSD之间，特别适用于“温数据”存储。随着AI和大数据应用的增加，原本用于冷数据存储的大型数据湖需要支持更活跃的工作负载，E2 SSDs应运而生。其设计基于高容量部署，尺寸为200mm x 76mm x 9.5mm，使用EDSFF接口和NVMe协议，通过PCIe 6.0连接，最大功耗80瓦。每个2U服务器可容纳多达40个E2 SSDs，总容量可达40PB。E2强调容量而非极致性能，目标是在成本和性能间取得平衡，预计2025年夏季推出。制造商如Micron和Pure Storage正推动这一标准，旨在降低总拥有成本并满足企业对大容量存储的需求。尽管不会立即取代HDD，但E2为温数据存储提供了具有竞争力的解决方案。

44139446.article_content:
Enterprise
SSD
Petabyte-Class E2 SSDs Poised to Disrupt Warm Data Storage
by
Andrew Waag
May 30, 2025
written by
Andrew Waag
May 30, 2025
E2 SSDs are poised to redefine high-capacity storage with up to 1PB per drive—bridging the gap between HDDs and high-performance flash.
Once reserved primarily for archival use, large-scale data lakes are now asked to support increasingly active workloads. New AI applications, analytics pipelines, and emerging digital services are driving up the “temperature” of previously considered cold data. The result is a growing middle ground, where data is accessed too frequently for HDDs to handle efficiently, but not hot enough to warrant the cost of performance SSDs. E2 is a new flash form factor to address this emerging “warm” storage tier. It is designed to bridge the gap between high-capacity hard drives and traditional enterprise SSDs, offering a more practical balance of performance, density, and cost.
The Storage Networking Industry Association (SNIA) and the Open Compute Project (OCP), two communities comprising some of the largest users, manufacturers, and standard maintainers of data center equipment, including (but not limited to) Meta, Microsoft, Micron, Pure Storage, Samsung, and Sandisk, have already designed and begun prototyping the new SSD form factor. Made from the ground up for high-capacity deployments in 2U servers, these new drives will feature up to one petabyte of QLC storage per device. They will reuse the industry standard EDSFF connector, as previously seen on E1 and E3 devices.
Physical Dimensions and Specifications
In an upright configuration, the physical size of each drive will be 200 millimeters (~7.9 inches) in length, and 76mm tall (~3 inches), with a thickness of only 9.5mm (~0.4 inches).
The E2 height and connector alignment specifications are derived from the E3 standard, while the indicator LED placement follows the E1 SSDs.
This size is ideal for dense storage servers, accommodating up to 40 E2 SSDs in a 2U node, which can translate to up to 40 PB in a single server. Drives communicate using the NVMe protocol over a generation 6 or higher PCIe 4-lane connection, and can use up to 80 watts of power per-SSD (although most drives are expected to run in the 20-30 watt range). This means a fully populated server could theoretically draw anywhere between 0.8 and 3.2 kilowatts just for storage! The thermal load resulting from a high-power configuration could present a significant challenge for traditional air-cooled designs, but such designs are unlikely.
From a performance perspective, E2 is targeting 8-10 MB/s per terabyte. Performance will be substantially higher than that of HDDs, reaching up to 10,000 MB/s for a one-petabyte drive. However, capacity is the ultimate goal of the E2 standard, as demonstrated by its massive 64 NAND package site support. For the intended use cases, the performance of E2 needs to be “good enough,” or said another way, for this class of storage, there’s no reason to pay more per TB than is absolutely required.

Manufacturer Motivations
Micron is a significant contributor to the E2 standard development and is likely to utilize it as a new tool in its battle against hard drives. With this new form factor, Open Compute Project engineers and designers aim to bridge the gap between the “fast but costly” SSDs and the “slow but affordable” HDD storage tiers, thereby reducing the total cost of ownership due to factors such as power, cooling, and longevity. A competitive middle-of-the-road solid-state option for high-capacity storage systems would also help boost sales of NAND packages and lower-tier controllers.
Pure Storage revealed a 300-terabyte E2 prototype on May 14 during the OCP Storage Tech Talk event. It features a large flash controller, six-piece DRAM caches, and numerous capacitors for safe buffer flushing in the event of unexpected power loss. Adopting the E2 standard would enable Pure to offer customers cost-effective “tier two” storage options, a solution desperately needed by organizations and businesses seeking to reduce costs while still reaping the benefits of SSDs.
Looking Ahead: Will the Industry Be Ready for E2?
The E2 form factor represents a practical, flash-based answer to the growing need for high-capacity “warm” storage. It won’t replace HDDs overnight, but the combination of petabyte-class capacity, sufficient performance, and dense 2U deployment makes it one of the more compelling recent developments in enterprise storage.

data.author: rizs12
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：开源软件贡献的动机和方式

不同观点：
• [em3rgent0rdr] 认为，开源软件提供的免费使用本身就是一种回报，贡献代码可以视为对这种回报的回馈。修复bug或添加功能不仅帮助了软件发展，也让自己受益。
• [acheong08] 指出，他们编写的许多代码经济价值不高，公开分享无妨，有时这些代码对其他人也有帮助。他们完全将项目维护交给社区，并从开源软件中个人获益。
• [ryao] 的贡献主要集中在修复bug上，动机是解决自己的需求或享受解决问题的智力挑战。他们过去曾将此作为全职工作，但现在每周只花几个小时。
• [dyingkneepad] 表示，尽管信仰开源模式，但每两周的薪水和健康保险等实际利益是主要动机，因为他们每天花费大量时间在开源项目上。
• [brynet] 开玩笑说，他们的动机是食物，特别是披萨。
• [deciduously] 提到，贡献是因为特定项目未能满足他们的特定需求，且他们知道如何修复。
• [horsellama] 列举了几个动机：修复困扰自己的bug、建立人脉和学习。
• [UncleEntity] 分享了他们在Blender项目的经验，最初是因为兴趣，后来通过解决bug和添加功能获得贡献者身份，过程中学到了很多技术。
• [m3047] 强调，贡献可以有多种形式，不限于提交PR。他们通过反馈、编写辅助工具和开发相关项目来贡献开源社区，但尚未找到志同道合的群体。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：[dyingkneepad] 提到的经济动机与其他参与者更理想化的动机形成对比，显示出开源贡献者社区中不同人的实际需求和理想目标之间的张力。
• 贡献方式多样性：从提交代码、修复bug到撰写文档和提供反馈，不同参与者展示了多种贡献开源项目的方式。
• 社区协作：[acheong08] 和 [m3047] 都提到了将项目交给社区维护的经验，显示了开源项目中协作和所有权转移的重要性。
• 个人受益：许多参与者提到，贡献开源项目不仅帮助了社区，也给他们自己带来了技术和个人方面的成长。

data.title: An Interactive Guide to Flexbox in CSS
data.author: cekrem
data.article_summary: 本文简要介绍了Flexbox的强大功能及其工作原理，通过一个无需媒体查询的动态布局示例，展示了Flexbox如何自动调整布局。文章强调了Flexbox的灵活性，可以控制子元素的增长、收缩及空间分配。尽管CSS Grid也很强大，但Flexbox在处理垂直或水平排列的动态UI时仍具优势。文章还讲解了Flexbox的关键概念，如主轴与交叉轴，以及如何通过`flex-direction`切换布局方向。最后，介绍了如何使用`justify-content`属性调整子元素在主轴上的分布。Flexbox的规则可以无缝应用于水平和垂直布局，非常适合需要灵活布局的设计。

In this blog post, I want to refine your mental model for Flexbox.

Introduction to Flexbox
CSS is comprised of many different layout algorithms, known officially as “layout modes”. Each layout mode is its own little sub-language within CSS. The default layout mode is
Flow layout
, but we can opt in to Flexbox by changing the
display
property on the parent container:

to
the
world
